title: The rate book (tarieven)
description: Nh1816 bromfietsverzekering, 2018-07-18 — vehicle-type codes, the age-category-to-BM-basis table, the 25-step bonus-malus ladder, WA premiums (5 categories x 4 vehicle types), casco premiums (31 catalog-value brackets x 5 categories x 4 vehicle types) and the one accident-cover combination this product prices. Everything below only looks things up in it.

title: Rating age (as of 1 January)
description: The source worksheet rates on the driver's age on 1 January of the tariff year, not on the tariff date itself — a deliberate policy-year stability choice. We derive '1 January' from the tariff date instead of TODAY(), so a run next year reproduces this output.

title: Eligibility age (as of the tariff date)
description: A separate, exact age — the source worksheet's 'too young' check compares the birth date to today directly, so this uses the tariff date rather than the 1-January age above.

title: Driver under 16
description: WA and casco are not rated at all below this age; the accident cover has no such guard in the source, so it stays unguarded here too.

title: Catalog value including accessories
description: The casco tables bracket on this combined value, not on the catalog value alone.

title: Risk category (age band)
description: 16 or younger is category A (also the source's own fallback for an unmapped age); five bands cover the rest. This collapses the worksheet's 115-row per-age lookup — every age in a band maps to the same category, so the band is the rule.

title: Vehicle type (from the SIVI object-sort code)
description: 62/63/60/13 are the codes this tariff prices; an unrecognised code falls back to Brommer, matching the source worksheet's own IFERROR default.

title: Casco catalog-value bracket
description: The casco tables price a value 'up to and including' 31 brackets; this is the ceiling-lookup the source worksheet does with an approximate-match HLOOKUP. Values above the top bracket are capped at it — the source's own acceptance rules would decline them outright, which is out of scope here (see the README).

title: Open the lookup node
description: One node holding every join key, so one resolve can fetch four tables at once.

title: Four tables, one command
description: BM basis by risk category, WA premium, casco premium and the accident-cover tariff — every rate this quote needs except the bonus-malus ladder itself, which needs the BM step this resolve is about to help compute.

title: Bonus-malus step
description: BM basis for the risk category, plus claim-free years, plus any extra steps, held inside the ladder's 1-25 range.

title: Bonus-malus ladder
description: A second resolve, because the BM step this joins on only exists after the first one ran.

title: WA — netto basis premie
description: Gross tariff premium, times the bonus-malus factor, with the tariff's standard 20% commission stripped back out. Zero if WA was not selected, or the driver is under 16.

title: Casco — netto basis premie
description: Same shape as WA, from the catalog-value-bracketed casco table.

title: Ongevallen inzittenden — netto basis premie
description: No bonus-malus factor on this cover, and the source worksheet requires WA to be selected too — accident cover is never sold standalone. No age guard either: the source does not gate this line on 'too young'.

title: Package discount factor
description: Discounts are stored as negative percentages, so 1 + pct/100 is already a reduction.

title: Advice discount factor
description: The source worksheet always applies this discount (its 'apply advice discount?' cell is hardcoded 'j' for every coverage) rather than asking per quote, so we do the same.

title: wa — netto product premie
description: Package, group and advice discount applied on top of the netto basis premie.

title: casco — netto product premie
description: Package, group and advice discount applied on top of the netto basis premie.

title: accidents — netto product premie
description: Package, group and advice discount applied on top of the netto basis premie.

title: Commission factor
description: The actual, agreed commission (0-38%) is added back on top of the netto product premie — this is what the source worksheet calls the 'totaal product premie'.

title: wa — totaal product premie
description: Netto product premie plus the agreed commission. This is what the AFD summary table calls 'bruto'.

title: casco — totaal product premie
description: Netto product premie plus the agreed commission. This is what the AFD summary table calls 'bruto'.

title: accidents — totaal product premie
description: Netto product premie plus the agreed commission. This is what the AFD summary table calls 'bruto'.

title: WA — assurantiebelasting
description: 21% over the totaal product premie.

title: Ongevallen inzittenden — assurantiebelasting
description: Exempt by law — a personal-accident cover, not a damage cover.

title: Netto basis premie (per term)
description: Every monthly amount above is scaled to the payment term the same way: sum, times months in the term, divided by 12.

title: Totaal product premie (per term)
description: The AFD summary table's 'bruto', totalled — includes the re-added commission, excludes tax.

title: Provisie (per term)
description: Totaal product premie minus netto product premie.

title: Totaal premie (per term)
description: What is actually collected each term.

title: Netto advies premie (per term, working figure)
description: Package and group discount only, no advice discount — the figure the source worksheet's advice-discount breakdown is measured against. Not itself part of the output; it only exists to produce the next line.

title: Advieskorting (bedrag, per term)
description: Negative, because a discount is a negative amount here, matching the source worksheet's own convention.

title: Premium per coverage
description: One object per coverage line, each with the same three figures the GIM output layer names Btp (bruto), Ntp (netto) and Tass (assurantiebelasting).

title: Policy summary (kassabon)
description: The receipt-style totals the source worksheet builds at the bottom of the calculation sheet, GIM field codes PP_NJP / PP_NTPEXCP / PP_NTPINKA / PP_TPP / PP_TASS / PP_TTOT / PP_TKRT — see the README for the full mapping.

title: Acceptance checks (OUT_..._Xg_Xm)
description: Every rule the source worksheet's Xg_Xm sheet still runs live — 22 of its 24 rows. Two are left out: msg 8 ('ouder dan 75 jaar') and msg 9 ('leeftijd minus schadevrije jaren') are hardcoded FALSE in the source itself, each with a note that the validation number and the message text disagree ('wat is hier de bedoeling? Bespreken met Paul W. voorlopig uitschakelen') — genuinely disabled pending a decision that was never made, not something this script should silently re-enable.

title: Acceptance decision
description: Declined if any Hard check fired; the one Soft check ('Bel 807', a suspicious postcode) never blocks acceptance on its own.

title: Acceptance messages
description: One row per rule, `active` true or false — the same shape as the source's own OUT_GimData_Contractdocument_Xg_Xm array, which lists every rule with an Active column rather than only the ones that fired. `shownToUser` false marks the rules the source annotated 'Geen validatie om aan de gebruiker te tonen' (WA verplicht, the three dekkingscode-length checks) — they still decide `acceptance.decision`, they are just not meant as customer-facing text.
